sources.title: Human History Map, imported Mon records and decoded Lower Myanmar outlines
sources.note: Own project factual-data exception. Three missing IDs, four decoded snapshots, identical tested Lower Myanmar coverage. Index intervals retained individually; full evidence in identity.json and point-checks.json. No historical ethnic or sovereign boundary inferred from polygon.

sources.title: Donald M. Stadtner, The Mon of Lower Burma (2008), Journal of the Siam Society 96
sources.note: Original scholarly PDF read directly. Pages 193-194 distinguish later conquest tradition from evidence of Mon influence; page 198 Winka monastery and disputed date of tablet WK 6, Mathias Jenny reading in footnote 4; page 202 Kyanzittha inscriptions including 1098; page 203 and figure 9 page 215 Mahajanaka scenes. The paper contests Aung-Thwin; its ethnic attribution of all archaeology is not adopted.

sources.title: Khin Ma Ma Mu, Terracotta Votive Tablets from Catubhummika Hngak Twin Monastery, Thaton (2018)
sources.note: Original journal abstract fully readable in indexed results; direct page fails. Reproducible exact-title query plus 1350. Original article text additionally indexed on ResearchGate, same work not separate budget. Abstract says over 2000 total and 1350 good condition; introduction says 1350 complete plus 2000 fragments, so no exact total asserted. Stylistic eighth/ninth-eleventh century range, no Mon/Pyu inscription in this particular assemblage.

sources.title: Kaushik Gangopadhyay and colleagues, Finding Historical Linkages between India and Myanmar through Archaeological and Physicochemical Analysis of Ceramics (2024)
sources.note: Original Cardiff repository manuscript read directly, pages 8-10 and Table 4 for Lower Myanmar ceramics; abstract and analysis for chemical comparisons. Entire study first century BCE to thirteenth century CE; limited site dating and no claim every pot belongs in 800-1279. Rice-husk FTIR suggestion not used as diet evidence. DOI 10.1016/j.jasrep.2024.104828.

sources.title: U Aung Myint and Elizabeth Moore, Finger-Marked Designs on Ancient Bricks in Myanmar (1991)
sources.note: Original scholarly PDF read directly. Pages 81 and 91-93, Kyaikkatha marks/aerial discovery and Thaton laterite-faced moat/1986 brick discoveries. Regionally widespread technology not ethnic fingerprint. Pyu rice-husk samples and Thagara evidence excluded.

sources.title: Elizabeth Moore, U San Win and Pyiet Phyo Kyaw, Water Management in the Urban Cultural Heritage of Myanmar (2016)
sources.note: Original full scholarly HTML read directly, Kyaikkatha section and Plate 3. Seasonal ponds, lake/reservoir chain, roughly one-kilometer canal. Authors explicitly state canal unexcavated/undated and infer first-millennium association from role in settlement. Later local lake names not assigned ancient dates. No household toilet inference.

sources.title: H. L. Shorto, The Kyaikmaraw Inscriptions (1958)
sources.note: Original publisher extract read directly: Kyaikmaraw I, Queen Baña Thau/Shin Sawbu land dedication 1455, earliest dated Middle Mon inscription in author assessment. Shrine southeast of Moulmein, outside imported polygon and after all atlas intervals; explicitly later comparison. No full-paywalled-text claim.

sources.title: British Library, Wat Cet Riw Collection, EAP1123/1
sources.note: Original archival description read directly: late nineteenth/early twentieth-century collection, three medical texts, Mon/Pali/Thai, accordion paper books, multiple hands and doodles, local migration memories and donor box dated 1918. That box date is not manuscript date. Modern Mon community in Samut Sakhon, Thailand, outside polygon.

proposedOverrides.summary: A shared regional history for three Lower Myanmar atlas records. Their repeated outline does not establish one continuously independent kingdom; local settlements, Pagan-era connections and later Mon communities are distinguished.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Shared regional narrative, explicitly not one continuously sovereign kingdom
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Four snapshots repeat the same Lower Myanmar coverage. Thaton, Winka, Bago, Kyaikkatha and Pathein are inside. Pagan, central Thai Dvaravati, Mawlamyine and Kawgun are outside. Site points and full decoded coordinates saved separately.
batchIdentityNotes.related: No Dvaravati or Pagan association. mon-states includes imported Thaton Kingdom hint, but later Mon label cannot establish continued Thaton independence. Hanthawaddy and living Mon communities explicitly later/distinct; no modern Mon State boundary substitution.
batchIdentityNotes.dateResolution: Original override spans retained; card includes the intervening 1000-1100 context as a gap in these map records, not a gap in settlement. No fabricated fall year or successor link.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Winka WK 6 actual Mon fragment, Jenny Roman transcription with gloss, disputed proposed sixth-century date explicitly disclosed. It does not claim securely contemporaneous 800-1279 words or pretend Roman letters reproduce original script.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No early household family-size, formal education system, menu, remedy or toilet evidence established. Monastic residences and pictorial religious narrative provide bounded daily/learning evidence; Thai-Mon medical books and migration memory are explicitly later comparative continuity.
